cards.text: Moses is still preaching to Israel and laying out God's laws. Now he turns to who may enter the assembly of the LORD. First up: no man whose private parts were crushed or cut off may enter.

cards.question: True or false: Moses says someone of illegitimate birth may not enter the assembly of the LORD, and neither may his descendants, even to the tenth generation.

cards.text: Then Moses names two whole nations. No Ammonite or Moabite may enter the assembly, even to the tenth generation, and he tells Israel exactly why.

cards.question: On Israel's way out of Egypt, the Ammonites and Moabites did not meet them with ___ and ___.
On top of that, who do the Ammonites and Moabites hire to curse Israel?

cards.text: They hire a man to curse Israel. Paid him and everything. And the LORD your God would not even listen to Balaam.

cards.question: Instead, the LORD turns Balaam's curse into a ___ for Israel.
Why does the LORD turn Balaam's curse into a blessing for Israel?

cards.text: That's like paying a guy to leave my bakery a one-star review and he walks out typing FIVE STARS. So Moses says Israel is not to seek peace or prosperity from Ammon and Moab as long as they live.
But two other neighbors get very different words. First, Moses says, Do not despise an Edomite.

cards.question: Why shouldn't Israel despise an Edomite?

answers.text: He fed Israel in the desert

cards.question: Next up is Egypt, and Moses says not to despise an Egyptian either. Why not?

answers.text: Israel lived as a foreigner in his land
Egypt made peace with Israel at the border
Egypt sent food after Israel in the desert

cards.question: Children born to Edomites and Egyptians may enter the assembly of the LORD in the ___ generation.

cards.text: Now Moses moves from the assembly to the army camp. When Israel is camped against their enemies, they're to keep themselves from every wicked thing.

cards.question: True or false: a man who becomes unclean because of a nocturnal emission may stay inside the camp.
After that man leaves the camp, when may he come back?

answers.text: At sunset after washing with water
After seven days outside the camp
After a priest looks him over

cards.text: Then Moses gets REAL practical: Israel needs a place outside the camp to relieve themselves, and a digging tool in their gear to dig a hole and cover it up. Yep, a digging tool, right there on the packing list.

cards.question: Why does Israel's camp need to be kept that clean?

answers.text: The LORD walks throughout the camp
Enemies could track them by it

cards.text: The LORD walks through the camp to protect them and deliver their enemies to them. When somebody important is coming over you clean behind the fridge, and this is the LORD HIMSELF.

cards.question: True or false: Moses says that if the LORD sees anything unclean in the camp, He could turn away from them.

cards.text: Then Moses talks about a slave who gets away from his master and takes refuge with Israel.

cards.question: True or false: Israel must return that slave to his master.
So where does the slave who took refuge with Israel get to live?

answers.text: In the town his master picks
In a town set apart for slaves

cards.text: And Moses adds, "Do not oppress him." Friend, after years in a junk drawer, I know what it means when somebody finally makes room for you.
Next, Moses says no daughter or son of Israel is to be a shrine prostitute.

cards.question: True or false: a prostitute's wages may be brought into the house of the LORD to fulfill a vow.
Why can't a prostitute's wages come into the house of the LORD?

answers.text: Both are detestable to the LORD
The priests would not accept it
The silver would not be pure

cards.text: Now money. Don't charge your brother interest, not on money, food or any other loan, so picture a credit card statement that just says, We're good, brother.

cards.question: So who MAY Israel charge interest?
If Israel doesn't charge a brother interest, the LORD their God may ___ them in everything they put their hand to in the land.

cards.text: Then Moses turns to vows. If you make a vow to the LORD your God, don't be slow to keep it.

cards.question: Why shouldn't anyone be slow to keep a vow to the LORD?

answers.text: The priests will write it down

cards.question: True or false: Moses says that if someone never makes a vow at all, they are guilty of sin.

cards.text: So be careful to follow through on what comes from your lips, because nobody made you say it. That's me telling a baker the boxes will be done by noon when nobody even ASKED for a time, and now I've got a deadline I made up all by myself.
Last, Moses takes Israel for a walk through a neighbor's vineyard.

cards.question: What may you do in your neighbor's vineyard?
True or false: you may also put some of your neighbor's grapes in your basket.
In your neighbor's grainfield, you may pluck the heads of grain with your ___, but you must not put a ___ to the grain.

cards.text: Grabbing a cookie off my cooling rack is one thing, but backing a TRUCK up to my bakery is another. And Moses isn't done preaching yet, friend, so stick around.

findings.problem: Moses appears here for the first time in the lesson, and the card never says who he is. It opens with 'Moses is still preaching to Israel' and gives no simple identifier.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: No story card sets up verse 2. Card 1 covers only verse 1, and the true or false statement restates verse 2 nearly word for word. The baker has nothing to reason from. The answer is either luck, or the statement's Bible-like detail ('even to the tenth generation') gives away that it is true.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: The card retells the hiring from verse 4 ('They hire a man to curse Israel. Paid him and everything.') but cites only Deuteronomy 23:5. The citation should be Deuteronomy 23:4-5. That opening line also just repeats what card 5 already covered, so it works as a recap instead of moving the passage forward.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: 'So Moses says Israel is not to seek peace or prosperity...' comes right after the joke about the curse turned into a blessing. That makes verse 6 sound like it follows from verse 5. The text never states that connection. Verse 6 follows the charges in verses 3-4.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates stop 1. It has 6 multiple choice cards, 3 true or false and 3 fill in the blank, so multiple choice appears twice as often as each other type.

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: The closing line 'Yep, a digging tool, right there on the packing list.' just restates the fact. It reads as a mild, pleasant aside, not a real laugh.

rule.text: When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: The right answer 'Both are detestable to the LORD' points to 'both', but no card has mentioned female or male prostitutes (verse 18). The baker can't tell what 'both' means. It also makes the right answer sound more like the Bible than the wrong answers.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: Deuteronomy 23 is a string of laws for everyday life: who may enter the assembly, camp hygiene, interest, vows, a neighbor's vineyard. That matches the long-stretch example 'rules for everyday life' (Exodus 21-23), which gets one summary card and no choice cards. But the passage is typed Sermons and sits inside Moses' second speech, and the docs say speeches and teaching are not long stretches. The walkthrough treats every law as a choice-worthy moment.
findings.question: When a law collection is delivered as part of a speech, as in Moses' speeches in Deuteronomy, does it count as a speech or teaching that gets full story and choice cards, or as a long stretch of rules for everyday life that gets one summary card?
